verses.text: “I make covenant with my eyes. So how I go look young woman with bad desire?
Because wetin be di share from God above and di inheritance from di Almighty on high?
No be disaster for di wicked and ruin for dem wey dey do wrong?
E no dey see my ways and count all my steps?
If I don waka with lies and my foot don hurry go deceit,
make dem weigh me for fair scale, so dat God go know my honesty,
if my step don turn from di way, if my heart don follow my eyes, if any dirt don stick to my hands,
den make I plant and make another person eat. Yes, make dem pull out di harvest of my field.
If woman don deceive my heart, if I don wait for my neighbor door,
den make my wife grind for another man, and make other men lie with am.
Because dat one go be terrible crime. Yes, na wrong wey judges go punish,
because na fire wey dey burn reach Abaddon and e go pull out all my increase.
If I don look down di case of my male servant or my female servant, when dem argue with me,
wetin I go do when God stand up? When e come, wetin I go answer am?
No be di one wey make me for belly make am too? No be one person form us for belly?
If I don stop di poor from wetin dem want or make di eyes of di widow fail,
or I don eat my food alone, and di orphan no eat from am,
because from my youth e grow with me like with papa, and I don guide di widow from my mama belly,
if I don see anybody dey perish because e no get clothes, or say di needy no get cover,
if im heart no bless me, if di wool of my sheep no warm am,
if I don lift my hand against di orphan because I see say my help dey for di gate,
den make my shoulder fall from di shoulder blade and my arm break from di bone.
Because disaster from God na terror to me. Because of im greatness, I no fit do anything.
If I don make gold my hope and talk to di fine gold say, ‘You be my confidence,’
if I don rejoice because my wealth big and because my hand don get plenty,
if I don look di sun when e dey shine or di moon wey dey move in beauty,
and my heart don secretly turn, and my hand don throw kiss from my mouth,
dis one too na wrong wey judges go punish, because I for don deny di God wey dey above.
If I don rejoice for di destruction of am wey hate me or lift myself up when evil find am,
yes, I no allow my mouth to sin by asking for im life with curse,
if di men of my tent no talk say, ‘Who fit find person wey no eat im fill of im meat?’
di stranger no sleep for di street, but I open my doors to di traveler,
if like Adam I don cover my wrongs by hiding my sin for my heart,
because I fear di big crowd and di shame of families frighten me, so dat I keep quiet and no go out of di door,
oh, if I get one to hear me! Look, na my signature be dis, make di Almighty answer me! Make my accuser write my charge!
Sure sure I go carry am for my shoulder. I go tie am on me like crown.
I go tell am di number of my steps. Like prince I go go near am.
If my land cry out against me and im furrows cry together,
if I don eat im fruits without money or cause im owners to lose dem life,
make thorns grow instead of wheat and bad weeds instead of barley.” Di words of Job don finish.
So dis three men stop to answer Job, because e dey righteous for im own eyes.
Den di anger of Elihu, Barachel pikin, di Buzite, of di family of Ram, burn against Job. Im anger burn because e dey defend imself pass God.
Im anger burn against im three friends too, because dem no find answer, yet dem don condemn Job.
Now Elihu don wait to talk to Job, because dem old pass am.
When Elihu see say no answer dey for di mouth of dis three men, im anger burn.
Elihu, Barachel pikin, di Buzite, answer say, “I young, and una very old. So I hold back and I no dare show una my opinion.
I talk say, ‘Make days talk, and make plenty years teach wisdom.’
But spirit dey inside man, and di breath of di Almighty dey give dem understanding.
No be di great dey wise, and no be di old dey understand justice.
So I talk say, ‘Listen to me, I go show my opinion too.’
Look, I wait for una words and I listen to una arguments, as una dey search out wetin to talk.
Yes, I give una my attention, and look, nobody among una convince Job or answer im words.
Take care, make una no talk say, ‘We don find wisdom.’ Na God fit refute am, no be man,
because e no direct im words against me, and I no go answer am with una speeches.
Dem dey shock. Dem no dey answer again. Dem no get word to talk.
I go wait because dem no dey talk, because dem dey stand still and no dey answer again?
I go answer my own part too. I go show my opinion too.
Because I full of words. Di spirit inside me dey push me.
Look, my chest like wine wey no get way out. Like new wineskins e ready to burst.
I go talk so dat I go feel better. I go open my lips and answer.
I beg una, make I no show favor to any man, and I no go flatter any man.
Because I no know how to flatter. If I do am, my Maker go quick take me away.”
“However, Job, I beg you, hear my speech and listen to all my words.
Look now, I don open my mouth. My tongue don talk inside my mouth.
My words dey come from di honesty of my heart. Wetin my lips know, dem dey talk am sincerely.
God Spirit don make me, and di breath of di Almighty dey give me life.
If you fit, answer me. Arrange your words before me and stand up.
Look, I dey before God like you. Dem form me from clay too.
Look, my terror no go frighten you, and my pressure no go heavy on you.
Sure sure you don talk for my hearing. I don hear di voice of your words, dey talk say,
‘I clean and I no get disobedience. I innocent, and no wrong dey inside me.
Look, e dey find reason against me. E dey count me as im enemy.
E dey put my feet inside stocks. E dey mark all my paths.’
Look, I go answer you. For dis one you no dey right, because God big pass man.
Why you dey fight am, since e no dey give account of any of im matters?
Because God dey talk one time, yes two times, even though man no dey pay attention.
For dream, for vision of di night, when deep sleep fall on men, for slumber on di bed,
den e dey open di ears of men and dey seal dem instruction,
so dat e go draw man back from im plan and hide pride from man.
E dey keep im soul back from di pit and im life from dying by di sword.
Dem dey correct am with pain on im bed too, and with constant fight for im bones,
so dat im life dey hate bread and im soul dey hate sweet food.
Im flesh don finish so tay dem no fit see am. Im bones wey dem no dey see before dey stick out.
Yes, im soul dey come near di pit and im life dey come near di destroyers.
If angel dey beside am, one interpreter, one among thousand, to show man wetin dey right for am,
den God go dey gracious to am and talk say, ‘Save am from going down to di pit. I don find ransom.’
Im flesh go fresh pass pikin own. E go return to di days of im youth.
E go pray to God, and God go dey kind to am, so dat e go see im face with joy. E go return to man im righteousness.
E dey sing before men and dey talk say, ‘I don sin and I don twist wetin right, and e no profit me.
E don buy back my soul from going into di pit. My life go see di light.’
Look, God dey do all dis things two times, yes three times, with man,
to bring back im soul from di pit, so dat light of di living go shine on am.
Mark am well, Job, listen to me. Keep quiet, and I go talk.
If you get anything to talk, answer me. Talk, because I wan show say you dey right.
If no, listen to me. Keep quiet, and I go teach you wisdom.”
Den Elihu answer say,
“Hear my words, una wise men. Give me ear, una wey get knowledge.
Because di ear dey test words, like how mouth dey taste food.
Make we choose wetin dey right for us. Make we know among ourselves wetin dey good.
Because Job don talk say, ‘I dey righteous, and God don take away my right.
Even with my right dem dey count me as liar. My wound no fit heal, even though I no get disobedience.’
Which man be like Job, wey dey drink mockery like water,
wey dey go with dem wey dey do wrong and dey waka with wicked men?
Because e don talk say, ‘E no profit man to enjoy God.’
So listen to me, una men wey get understanding. E far from God to do wickedness, from di Almighty to do wrong.
Because e go pay man back for im work and make every man find according to im ways.
Yes, sure sure God no go do wickedness, and di Almighty no go twist justice.
Who put am over di earth? Or who appoint am over all di world?
If e set im heart on imself, if e gather im spirit and im breath to imself,
all flesh go perish together, and man go return to dust.
If you get understanding now, hear dis. Listen to di voice of my words.
Person wey hate justice fit rule? You go condemn di one wey dey righteous and mighty?
E good to talk to king say, ‘You dey wicked,’ or to nobles say, ‘You dey ungodly,’
di one wey no dey show favor to princes and no dey respect di rich pass di poor? Because all of dem na work of im hands.
For one moment dem dey die, even for midnight. Di people dey shake and dey pass away. Dem dey take di mighty away without hand.
Because im eyes dey on di ways of man. E dey see all im steps.
No darkness or thick gloom dey where di wrongdoers fit hide.
Because e no need to look man again, say e go go before God for judgment.
E dey break mighty men to pieces for ways wey nobody fit find out and dey set others for dem place.
Because e know dem works, e dey overturn dem for night, so dat dem dey destroyed.
E dey strike dem like wicked men for di open sight of others,
because dem turn from following am and no consider any of im ways,
so dat dem make di cry of di poor reach am. E hear di cry of di suffering.
When e give quietness, who fit condemn? When e hide im face, who fit see am? Whether na nation or man, na di same,
so dat di godless man no go rule and nobody go dey to trap di people.
Because any man don talk to God say, ‘I don bear correction. I no go offend again.
Teach me wetin I no see. If I don do wrong, I no go do am again’?
Im payment go be as you want, say you reject am? Because na you go choose, no be me. So talk wetin you know.
Men wey get understanding go tell me, yes, every wise man wey hear me,
‘Job dey talk without knowledge. Im words no get wisdom.’
I wish say dem test Job to di end, because of how e dey answer like wicked men.
Because e dey add rebellion to im sin. E dey clap im hands among us and dey increase im words against God.”
Den Elihu answer say,
“You think say dis na your right, or you dey talk say, ‘My righteousness pass God own,’
say you dey ask, ‘Wetin go be di advantage for you? Wetin I go gain more than if I sin?’
I go answer you and your friends wey dey with you.
Look up to di heavens and see. See di skies, wey high pass you.
If you don sin, wetin you fit do against am? If your wrongs plenty, wetin you do am?
If you dey righteous, wetin you give am? Or wetin e receive from your hand?
Your wickedness fit hurt man like you, and your righteousness fit profit son of man.
Because of di plenty oppression dem dey cry out. Dem dey cry for help because of di arm of di mighty.
But nobody dey talk say, ‘Where God my Maker dey, wey dey give songs for night,
wey dey teach us more than di animals of di earth and make us wiser than di birds of di sky?’
Dere dem dey cry, but nobody dey answer, because of di pride of evil men.
Sure sure God no go hear empty cry, and di Almighty no go pay attention to am.
How much less when you dey talk say you no see am. Di case dey before am, and you dey wait for am.
But now, because e never visit for anger and e no dey pay plenty attention to pride,
so Job dey open im mouth with empty talk and e dey increase words without knowledge.”
Elihu continue and talk say,
“Bear with me small, and I go show you, because I still get something to talk for God side.
I go get my knowledge from far and give righteousness to my Maker.
Because true true my words no be lie. Person wey perfect for knowledge dey with you.
Look, God mighty and no dey despise anybody. E mighty for strength of understanding.
E no dey keep di life of di wicked, but e dey give di suffering dem right.
E no dey take im eyes from di righteous, but with kings for di throne e dey set dem forever, and dem dey lifted up.
If dem tie dem with chains and dem catch dem with ropes of suffering,
den e dey show dem dem work and dem wrongs, say dem don behave proud.
E dey open dem ear to instruction too and dey command say make dem return from wickedness.
If dem listen and serve am, dem go spend dem days for good fortune and dem years for pleasure.
But if dem no listen, dem go perish by sword. Dem go die without knowledge.
But dem wey godless for heart dey store anger. Dem no dey cry for help when e tie dem.
Dem dey die for youth. Dem life dey perish among di unclean.
E dey save di suffering by dem suffering and dey open dem ear for oppression.
Yes, e for don draw you out of trouble, into wide place wey no get limit. Wetin dem put for your table for dey full of fat.
But you full of di judgment of di wicked. Judgment and justice don hold you.
No make anger tempt you to scoff, and no make di greatness of di ransom turn you aside.
Your wealth go support you for trouble, or all di might of your strength?
No long for night, when people dey cut off for dem place.
Take care. No turn to wickedness, because you don choose dis pass suffering.
Look, God dey lifted up for im power. Who be teacher like am?
Who don set im way for am? Or who fit talk say, ‘You don do wickedness’?
Remember say you dey praise im work, wey men don sing about.
All men don look am. Man dey see am from far.
Look, God great, and we no know am. Di number of im years no fit search out.
Because e dey draw up di drops of water, wey dey fall as rain from im mist,
wey di skies dey pour down and drop on man plenty.
Yes, anybody fit understand how di clouds dey spread, di thunder of im tent?
Look, e dey spread im light round am. E dey cover di bottom of di sea.
Because by dis ones e dey judge di peoples. E dey give food plenty.
E dey cover im hands with lightning and dey command am to strike di target.
Im noise dey tell about am, and di animals too about di storm wey dey come up.”
“Yes, for dis one my heart dey tremble and move from im place.
Hear, oh, hear di noise of im voice, di sound wey dey come out of im mouth.
E dey send am out under all di sky and im lightning to di ends of di earth.
After am voice dey roar, e dey thunder with di voice of im majesty. E no dey hold back di lightnings when dem hear im voice.
God dey thunder wonderfully with im voice. E dey do great things wey we no fit understand.
Because e dey talk to di snow say, ‘Fall for di earth,’ and to di shower and di big rain of im strength too.
E dey seal up di hand of every man, so dat all men wey e make go know am.
Den di animals dey go inside dem dens and dey stay for dem holes.
Out of im room di storm dey come, and cold from di north.
By di breath of God, ice dey form, and di width of di waters dey freeze.
Yes, e dey load di thick cloud with water. E dey spread di cloud of im lightning.
E dey turn round by im guidance, so dat dem go do anything wey e command dem for di face of di world,
whether na for correction, or for im land, or for faithful love, e dey make am come.
Listen to dis, Job. Stand still and think about di wonderful works of God.
You know how God dey control dem and make di lightning of im cloud shine?
You know how di clouds dey balance, di wonderful works of di one wey perfect for knowledge?
You wey your clothes warm, when di earth quiet because of di south wind?
You fit, with am, spread out di sky, wey strong like cast metal mirror?
Teach us wetin we go tell am, because we no fit arrange our speech because of darkness.
Dem go tell am say I wan talk? Or man go wish say dem swallow am?
Now men no dey see di light wey bright for di skies, when di wind don pass and clear dem.
From di north golden shine dey come. Fearful majesty dey with God.
We no fit reach di Almighty. E dey lifted up for power. For justice and great righteousness, e no go oppress.
So men dey fear am. E no dey look any wey wise for heart.”
Den di Lord answer Job out of di whirlwind say,
“Who be dis one wey dey darken advice with words without knowledge?
Tie your waist like man, because I go ask you, den you go answer me!
Where you dey when I lay di foundations of di earth? Talk, if you get understanding.
Who set im measures, if you know, or who stretch di line on am?
Wetin dem fasten im foundations on? Or who lay im cornerstone,
when di morning stars sing together, and all di sons of God shout for joy?
Or who close di sea with doors, when e break out from di womb,
when I make clouds im cloth and wrap am with thick darkness,
mark out my boundary for am and set bars and doors,
and talk say, ‘You fit come here, but no go further. Here your proud waves go stop’?
You don command di morning for your days and make di dawn know im place,
so dat e go hold di ends of di earth and shake di wicked out of am?
E dey change like clay under di seal and dey stand out like cloth.
From di wicked, dem dey hold back dem light. Di high arm dey broken.
You don enter di springs of di sea? Or you don waka for di hidden places of di deep?
Dem don show you di gates of death? Or you don see di gates of di shadow of death?
You don understand di earth for im width? Talk, if you know all.
Which way go di home of light? As for darkness, where im place dey,
so dat you go carry am go im boundary and know di paths to im house?
Sure sure you know, because dem born you den, and di number of your days plenty!
You don enter di store rooms of di snow? Or you don see di store rooms of di hail,
wey I don keep for di time of trouble, for di day of battle and war?
Which way dem dey share di lightning, or di east wind dey scatter for di earth?
Who don cut channel for di flood or way for di thunder storm,
to make am rain for land where nobody dey, for di wilderness where nobody dey,
to satisfy di waste and empty ground and make di tender grass spring up?
Rain get papa? Or who be papa of di drops of dew?
From whose womb ice dey come? Di gray frost of di sky, who born am?
Di waters dey turn hard like stone, when di face of di deep freeze.
You fit tie di group of di Pleiades or loosen di ropes of Orion?
You fit lead out di constellations for dem season? Or you fit guide di Bear with im cubs?
You know di laws of di heavens? You fit set up dem rule over di earth?
You fit lift your voice to di clouds, so dat plenty water go cover you?
You fit send out lightnings, so dat dem go go? Dem go report to you say, ‘We dey here’?
Who don put wisdom for di inside? Or who don give understanding to di mind?
Who fit count di clouds by wisdom? Or who fit pour out di bottles of di sky,
when di dust run together become lump and di clods stick together?
You fit hunt prey for di lioness or satisfy di hunger of di young lions,
when dem bend down for dem dens and wait inside di bush?
Who dey provide food for di raven, when im young ones cry to God and wander because dem no get food?”
